name: Gabapentin
lead: Gabapentin is a prescription anticonvulsant and analgesic that is structurally related to the neurotransmitter GABA but, according to its US label, has no effect on GABA binding, uptake or degradation. It is sold under brand names including Neurontin and Gralise [1][2]. The US label lists management of postherpetic neuralgia and adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures as its approved uses [2].

In looksmaxxing and recovery discussions it appears mainly as a drug taken off-label for sleep or anxiety. Published trials have mostly examined it in neuropathic pain, restless legs syndrome and epilepsy; no published trial has tested it for appearance outcomes, and evidence for sleep and anxiety use outside those conditions is described as limited in the reference literature [1][3].

Reference sources describe dizziness and somnolence as common adverse effects, and note misuse potential, particularly alongside opioids or sedatives. Its US controlled-substance status is unscheduled at the federal level, although some jurisdictions impose additional controls [1][2].
infobox: Prescription-only; not federally scheduled in the US, some jurisdictions add controls [1]

paras: The US label for gabapentin capsules lists management of postherpetic neuralgia in adults and adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures in adults and children aged three and over [2]. Grokipedia reports the original FDA approval in 1993 and the postherpetic neuralgia indication in 2002 [1]. A related prodrug, gabapentin enacarbil (Horizant), has its own approvals, including for restless legs syndrome [1].

Off-label prescribing is widespread. Reference sources list diabetic neuropathy, fibromyalgia, restless legs syndrome, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, migraine prophylaxis and alcohol withdrawal, and say evidence for several psychiatric uses is limited or inconsistent [1].

Gabapentin binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, a finding reported in a 1996 study of the drug [4]. The label states that the precise mechanisms of its analgesic and antiepileptic actions are unknown [2]. Later research proposed that the alpha-2-delta-1 protein also acts as a neuronal receptor for thrombospondins involved in excitatory synapse formation [5].
Grokipedia gives oral bioavailability as 27-60 percent (decreasing as the amount taken rises), negligible protein binding, no significant metabolism, renal excretion and a half-life of 5-7 hours [1].

The label lists dizziness and somnolence among the most common reactions and warns of driving impairment [2]. Serious adverse reactions named in the label include DRESS (multiorgan hypersensitivity), anaphylaxis and angioedema [2]. The label also describes a pregnancy exposure registry for antiepileptic drugs [2].
Grokipedia reports potential for misuse, especially in people with substance-use histories and when combined with opioids or benzodiazepines, with overdose and dependence risks [1].

Gabapentin is a generic medication with a long history as a prescription product; Grokipedia describes the US as not scheduling it federally while some jurisdictions apply controls [1]. In online recovery and sleep discussions it is mentioned as one of several prescription drugs people take off-label for sleep. The wiki found no community threads about it that could be cited, and no published study has examined it for looksmaxxing goals.

Randomized trials in 1998 reported on gabapentin for painful diabetic neuropathy and for postherpetic neuralgia [6][7]. Systematic reviews and guidelines on neuropathic pain, including a 2015 meta-analysis, evaluate gabapentin among first-line options [8]. Registered trials have examined gabapentin enacarbil in restless legs syndrome and alcohol use disorder, and gabapentin formulations for post-surgical and post-amputation pain [9][10][11]. No studies were found testing gabapentin for appearance outcomes, and no trial identified here assessed it as a sleep aid in otherwise healthy people.

card.summary: A prescription nerve-pain and seizure drug that some people take off-label for sleep; proven for neuropathic pain, untested for looks.
card.note: Prescription-only; sedation, dizziness and misuse risk, especially with opioids or sedatives.

quick.overview:
Gabapentin is a prescription anticonvulsant approved in the US for postherpetic neuralgia and as add-on therapy for partial seizures. It is also prescribed off-label for many other conditions.

In looksmaxxing and recovery circles it is discussed as a possible sleep or anxiety aid. No published trial has tested it for appearance, and evidence for psychiatric use is described as limited.
quick.mechanism: It binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, which reduces release of excitatory neurotransmitters. Despite resembling GABA, it does not act on GABA binding, according to its label; the exact mechanism is unknown.
quick.risks: The label lists dizziness, somnolence and driving impairment, plus rare serious hypersensitivity reactions. Reference sources report misuse potential, especially combined with opioids or benzodiazepines. It is prescription-only.
